entries.title: Apollo Passive Seismic Experiment observations
entries.mission: Apollo 12 and the wider Apollo PSE network
entries.instrument: Passive Seismic Experiment (PSE), channel XA.S12.00.MHZ in the featured sample
entries.period: The featured file is identified by its archive path as year 1969, day 323; the wider PSE collection spans Apollo observations from 1969–1977.
entries.units: The current browser parser does not read calibration metadata or reliably establish physical units. The plotted value-column header is shown, but units must be checked against the original PDS labels and StationXML before scientific interpretation.
entries.processing: The browser parses the selected PDS ASCII GeoCSV, heuristically selects a numeric observation column, plots up to 1,600 evenly sampled points for readability, and calculates descriptive statistics from all valid parsed values.
entries.limitations: Not a live feed. The parser does not apply instrument calibration, identify moonquakes, classify events, or assign physical meaning to peaks. Remote loading may fail because of browser cross-origin policy; downloading the original file and selecting it locally is supported.
entries.sourceLabel: NASA Planetary Data System — Apollo Seismic Data bundle

additionalSources.label: NASA PDS — Apollo 12 PSE instrument metadata

entries.title: Apollo passive-seismic station locator
entries.period: Stations deployed from 1969 to 1972; PSE operations continued until mid-1977.
entries.units: Latitude and longitude in degrees; instrument sampling rates in samples per second (Hz).
entries.processing: Published station coordinates are stored in data/alsep-network.json and plotted on a custom simplified near-side locator. The PSE sampling rates are displayed as instrument metadata.
entries.limitations: The locator is not a terrain map, geodetic projection, or raw seismic plot. Coordinates are rounded for this educational view. Sampling rates describe instrument metadata, not values measured in the displayed locator.
entries.sourceLabel: NASA PDS — Apollo 12 PSE instrument metadata

additionalSources.label: NASA NTRS — ALSEP data restoration and archiving

entries.title: NASA InSight instrument profiles
entries.period: Mission landed 26 November 2018; final communication 15 December 2022.
entries.units: Only units explicitly stated in the cited NASA instrument documentation are displayed in the profile facts. No time-series measurement is plotted.
entries.processing: Facts in data/insight-instruments.json are curated into interactive profiles. The adjacent spacecraft drawing is an original educational schematic and is labelled not to scale.
entries.limitations: This is not live telemetry, a measured instrument trace, a NASA-provided technical drawing, or a scale engineering model.

entries.title: 2026 NASA archive-release index
entries.kind: Editorial summaries of NASA release announcements
entries.mission: Voyager 2, New Horizons, Artemis II and Swift
entries.instrument: Varies by release; see each linked NASA announcement and archive.
entries.period: The observation period is shown separately on each release card and must not be confused with its publication date.
entries.units: Not applicable to the summary cards. Units belong to the underlying dataset documentation.
entries.processing: The cards in data/nasa-2026-releases.json summarize NASA Science Data Portal announcements and link to the corresponding archive or DOI.
entries.limitations: No underlying measurement arrays are embedded in these cards. A release announcement is not itself a dataset and its publication date is not the observation date.
entries.sourceLabel: NASA Science Data Portal — 2026 release announcements

entries.title: NASA Image and Video Library search
entries.mission: Depends on the visitor's search query
entries.instrument: Not applicable — image and video archive records
entries.processing: The browser requests search results from NASA's public images API and displays selected media metadata with a link to the individual NASA record.
entries.limitations: A search result is not automatically a science dataset or proof of image reuse rights. Check each individual record for creator credits and any third-party restrictions before reusing media.
